scenes.heading: Phylogenetic trees
scenes.sub: Who is related to whom, and how do we know?
scenes.say: A phylogenetic tree shows how species are related through shared ancestors. Scientists build them from body structures and DNA, and use the same methods to trace disease outbreaks.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: One LEGO kit built into a crane, a boat, a plane and a car
scenes.science: Homologous forelimbs: same bones, different jobs
scenes.breaks: the friends chose what to build, but no one designs a flipper; change comes from natural selection over many generations.
scenes.say: Give the same LEGO kit to four friends, and they build a crane, a boat, a plane and a car. Different jobs, same pieces. That's homologous structures. Human arms, whale flippers, bat wings and cat legs share the same bones, inherited from a common ancestor.

scenes.heading: Homologous vs analogous
scenes.say: Homologous means same build, different job, from divergent evolution. Analogous means same job, different build, like bird and insect wings, from convergent evolution. Only homologous structures show shared ancestry. Vestigial structures, like a whale's tiny pelvic bones, are leftovers from ancestors.

scenes.heading: Molecular evidence
points: Compare DNA or amino acid sequences
scenes.say: Molecular evidence compares DNA or amino acid sequences. After lineages split, each builds up its own mutations. So fewer differences means a fresher split. If differences pile up at a roughly steady rate, the molecular clock can estimate when lineages diverged.

scenes.heading: Reading a tree
points: Closest relatives share the nearest node
Read nodes, not the order of names
Clade: an ancestor and ALL descendants
scenes.say: Each node is a most recent common ancestor. Two species are closest when their shared node is nearest the tips. Don't judge by the order of names. Branches spin like a mobile. And a clade is an ancestor and all its descendants: snip one branch, and everything that falls off is a clade.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Gene differences: P–Q 1, P–R 4, Q–R 3, P–S 8, Q–S 7, R–S 4. Build the tree.
lines: Fewest: P and Q (1), join first
Next: R joins the P–Q pair
S is most different: joins at the root
scenes.say: P and Q differ by only one, so they join first. R differs from them by three and four, fewer than S, so R joins next. S is most different, so it branches off at the root. P and Q share the most recent common ancestor.

Quick recap. Homologous structures show common ancestry. Fewer sequence differences means a more recent common ancestor. Judge relatedness by nodes, and a clade is an ancestor with all its descendants. Now try the practice questions!
